<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par145 />''the people''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָֽעֵדָה|translate=all the congregation}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=5}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=40}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=עַם}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=47}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=קָהָל|translate=assembly}}. Cf. also the construction of national names, as {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָם}} ({{GHGpar|122|i}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּנֻ֫סוּ אֲרָם|translate=and the Syrians fled}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=5}}.—(β) with the predicate following, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן וּבָקָר|translate=sheep and oxen}}, construed with the plural in the following relative clause; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּקָר הָיוּ חֹֽרְשׁוֹת|translate=the cattle}} (cows) ''were ploughing''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=1}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=10|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫יִת}}=''family'' (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית שֶׁ֫מֶשׁ}} on the analogy of names of countries, is used for ''the inhabitants of Bethshemesh''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=11|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=4|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=עַם}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=חַיָּה|translate=herd}} [if correct, figuratively for ''people'']; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=נְבֵלָה|translate=dead bodies}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=קָצִיר|translate=boughs}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרָאֵל}}, preceded by a predicate in the singular.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|d}}
(''b'') Of substantives occasionally used as collectives: (α) with the predicate preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=זָכָר}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=55}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=10|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=רֹמֵס|translate=the treader down}}.—(β) with the predicate following, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אַחֵר}}=''others''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=סָתוּם|translate=a secret}}; [{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=7}}, and even after {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=19}}.]

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|e}}
(''c'') Of feminines as collective terms denoting masculine persons: (α) with the predicate preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=46}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיֵדְעוּ כָּל־הָאָרֶץ|translate=that all the earth may know}}, the i.e. all the inhabitants of the earth; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=66|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=96|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, 9, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵרִית|translate=remnant}}; ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָאָ֫רֶץ}}).—(β) with the predicate following, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=57}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=מוֹלֶ֫דֶת|translate=issue}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־מַרְבִּית|translate=all the increase}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=פִּרְחָח|translate=rabble}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=7}} read {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֻדֹת}} with the LXX.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|f}}
Examples of predicates in the singular, notwithstanding the collective meaning of the subject, occur in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=39}}, &c.—For examples of bold enallage of the number in noun-clauses with a substantival predicate, see above, {{GHGpar|141|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|g}}
Rem. Not infrequently the construction begins in the singular (especially when the predicate precedes; see o below), but is carried on, after the collective subject has been mentioned, in the plural; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=מְאֹד וַיִּ֫רֶב הָעָם וַיַּֽעַצְמוּ|translate=and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty}}; 33:4.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|h}}
'''3.''' On the other hand, plurals which have a singular meaning ({{GHGpar|124|a}}) are frequently construed with the singular, especially the ''pluralis excellentiae'' or ''maiestatis'' (§ g–i; on the union of these plurals with attributes, cf. {{GHGpar|132|h}}), as {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=1}}, 3, &c. (but see the Rem.), {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים|translate=master}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָלִים|translate=master, owner}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=29}}; cf., moreover, {{GHGheb|text=פָּנִים}} with the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַֽחֲמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=10}}.—So feminine forms with a masculine meaning are construed with a masculine predicate, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה קֹהֶ֫לֶת חָכָם|translate=the preacher was wise}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|i}}
Rem. The construction of {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים|translate=God}} with the plural of the predicate may be explained (apart of course from such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, where the speakers are heathen, and {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} may, therefore, be a numerical plural) partly as an acquiescence in a polytheistic form of expression, partly from the peculiar usage of one of the early documents of the Hexateuch, called ''E'' by Wellhausen, &c., ''B'' by Dillmann; cf. his commentary on Numbers—Joshua, p. 618, and above, {{GHGpar|124|g}}, note 2. So {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13}} (but in conversation with a heathen); 31:53, 35:7, cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=19}}. That this construction was afterwards studiously avoided from fear of misconception, is shown by such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=18}} compared with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=4}}, 8, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=17|verse=21}} compared with {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=7|verse=23}}. Cf. Strack’s excursus on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gen|chapter=20|verse=13}} in {{GHGcite|title=Die Genesis}}, Munich, 1905, p. 77.
